unit.title: Statistics: Tally Charts and Frequency Tables
unit.blurb: Collecting data with tally marks, counting tallies, and reading and completing frequency tables to answer questions.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Record data using tally marks and count tallies in groups of five.

O2.t: Complete and interpret frequency tables to answer questions.

p: When we collect data we make a **tally mark** for each answer: |, ||, |||, ||||.
The fifth mark goes **across** the first four to make a group of five: ||||/ . Then we count in fives.
Grouping tally marks in fives (four lines and one across) lets us count quickly in 5s and makes mistakes easier to spot.

lesson.q: A tally shows two full gates and 3 more marks. What number is it?

p: Make one mark for each item.
Draw the 5th mark across the four before it.
Count in fives, then add the extra marks.
The fifth tally mark crosses the other four, so each group is 5, not 4.

q.prompt: Before you read on: what number does |||| ||| show?

options.fb: Correct.
The crossed group is 5.

p: A **frequency table** shows how many times each answer was given. **Frequency** means 'how many'.
We can use it to answer questions: which was most popular? How many more chose red than blue? How many altogether?
A frequency table says how many of each. Adding the frequencies must give the number of things counted, which is a good check.

lesson.q: Favourite fruit: apple 7, banana 5, mango 8. How many children were asked? Which fruit is most popular?

p: Read across each row: item and how many.
Add all the frequencies to find the total.
Compare frequencies to find most or least.
Put your finger on the label first, then read the number next to it.
